newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says will assert itself in Africa bank.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says will assert itself in Africa bank.

text.p: Finance Minister Anthony Ani alleged in remarks published on Tuesday that Nigeria was being marginalised in the African Development Bank and that it would assert itself as the biggest shareholder of the lending agency.

"Nigeria is not being been given its proper due commensurate with the 10.4 percent shareholding in AfDB," he told the independent Guardian newspaper in an interview ahead of the annual meeting of the bank in Abidjan on Wednesday.
"It would appear that there is a deliberate attempt to exclude Nigeria. I don't know for what reason but whether they like it or not Nigeria is a factor in AfDB," Ani said.

Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation, is currently not on good terms with Western nations, which have pushed through major restructuring of the bank before they replenish the capital it badly needs for soft lending to the poor nations of the continent.
Nigeria is shunned by the West because of its slow pace of democratisation and alleged human rights violation, factors that have affected its relations in other areas.
The bank's new chief executive Mohammed Kabbaj was elected to the post after Nigeria compromised on fielding its own candidate.
Ani said: "We supported and ensured the victory of Mr Kabbaj on seven conditionalities and platforms. Unfortunately, these conditions have not been fulfilled."
Among the conditions were that Nigeria be given the vice-presidency of the bank and four directors but no Nigerian was currently a director, he said.
"It is a concerted effort, an international conspiracy against Nigeria," he said.
Bank officials have forecast a rise of about 60 percent in net income for 1997 following a 50 percent rise in 1996 compared to 1995 and attribute the improvement to its restructuring.
Ani said Nigeria would continue to canvass that non-African nations should not increase their current holding which totals 33 1/3 percent of the bank.
"We believe that the AfDB is an African institution and should maintain its Africanness," he said.
